name: Mellows Bridge
facts: Mellows Bridge, Dublin’s oldest still‑in‑use bridge, was originally built as Arran Bridge in 1683 and survived a catastrophic flood in 1763 that swept it away, prompting a grand redesign.
The 1768 replacement, designed by Charles Vallancey, featured three elegant elliptical stone arches spanning 42 m, a testament to 18th‑century engineering prowess on the River Liffey.
Renamed Queen Maeve Bridge in 1922 and later Liam Mellows Bridge in 1942, the structure reflects Ireland’s shifting political landscape while its cast‑iron balustrades were added in 1816–1818.
